panels.title: HEALTH — Commit Plugin & Merkle Root Processor

options.content: Every panel below is one check from `docs/runbooks/commit-plugin-health.md`'s checklist, filtered by the `$destChain` / `$sourceChain` template variables above. All metrics here are Beholder-ingested (see `commit/metrics/prom.go`) unless noted — set the `DS_PROMETHEUS` dashboard datasource variable to whichever Grafana datasource serves your Beholder pipeline before relying on this. **Grafana can't express the empty-result rule** (an empty result means UNKNOWN for `always_emitted: true` checks, OK for `always_emitted: false` checks) — a blank panel here means "go re-read that check's row in the checklist," not "assume healthy." Full rationale: `docs/runbooks/commit-plugin-health.md`.

`heartbeat_observation`/`heartbeat_outcome` first — if either is 0, every other panel's OK-looking value in this run is suspect. Windows are `[1m]` for the two heartbeats specifically because `rate()` extrapolates across its whole window: a `[5m]` window was measured to keep reporting "alive" for up to 5 minutes after a real outage (see the runbook's rate()-detection-lag note) — don't widen these without re-testing against a forced failure.

panels.description: always_emitted: true. crit_if result==0, ok_if result>0. Unconditional per-round liveness signal for Observation(); 0 or empty means every other check below may simply be stale, not bad. MAGNITUDE ISN'T MEANINGFUL: this is rate(counter[1m]) on a counter incremented once per OCR round, so a nonzero value like 0.5 just reflects this DON's round cadence, not '50% healthy' -- don't compare it across chains/environments or expect a specific number. The only threshold that matters is exactly 0 (dead) vs strictly >0 (alive).
panels.title: heartbeat_observation

panels.description: always_emitted: true. crit_if result==0, ok_if result>0. Same signal for Outcome(); flat while observation is healthy means OCR is failing to schedule/deliver to the outcome stage. Same 'magnitude isn't meaningful, only zero-vs-nonzero is' caveat as heartbeat_observation.
panels.title: heartbeat_outcome

panels.description: always_emitted: true. crit_if result==1, ok_if result==0. Home-chain config digest differs from the offramp's; root cause for a wide range of downstream rejections. Filtered to == 1 so only mismatched destChainID(s) appear as rows -- if $destChain matches more than one chain (multi-select/All), a bare max() collapses which chain mismatched; this table doesn't. No rows (including when nothing at all is selected) renders 'NO MISMATCH', which is the OK state here, not UNKNOWN.
panels.title: config_digest_mismatch — mismatched chains only

panels.description: always_emitted: false. warn_if any series>0, ok_if all series==0 (including empty result). Generic TrackedProcessor error counter; does not include swallowed per-goroutine failures (see merkleroot_observation_errors). STRAGGLER BUG (confirmed in commit/metrics/prom.go): this metric's Beholder counter (bhProcessorErrors) is registered but never actually incremented -- TrackProcessorLatency's error branch only calls the promauto counter, which still uses the OLD label scheme (chainFamily,chainID, not destChainID). This query intentionally keeps the old `chainID` label since `destChainID` would never match any series -- but on a datasource fed purely from Beholder/OTel (no promauto scrape), this panel will ALWAYS read empty/OK regardless of real errors. Treat as unreliable until bhProcessorErrors is actually called in code.
panels.title: processor_errors

panels.description: always_emitted: true. info only — single point-in-time sample with nothing to trend against. If pinned at the highest bucket, real latency likely exceeds it; still don't elevate to WARN/CRIT, there is no defined SLO. UNIT: this histogram is recorded in NANOSECONDS (time.Duration cast straight to float64 in commit/metrics/prom.go) -- confirmed by live testing on staging that displaying it with a 'seconds' unit renders a real 20s bucket value as ~634 YEARS. This panel's unit is set to 'ns' (Grafana auto-scales ns/us/ms/s), not 's' -- do not change it to 's' without dividing the query by 1e9 first.
panels.title: processor_latency_p95

options.content: Per source chain (`$sourceChain` regex) **and** destination chain (`$destChain`) — every query below filters both `sourceChainName` and `destChainID`, from `sourceChainAttrs()`/`destChainAttrs()` in `commit/metrics/prom.go`. The dest-chain filter was added after staging testing found these metrics carried no destination-chain label at all: two plugin instances for different dest chains reading the same source chain used to emit identical label sets and collide into one series. `seqnum_invariant_violation` and `offramp_lane_status="rmn_misconfigured"` are the only CRITs here — both explicitly documented in-code as stall/config-drift signals, not routine noise. `pending_messages` and `offramp_lane_status` are `always_emitted: true`; don't read an empty result for either as "no lanes, nothing to worry about."

panels.description: always_emitted: true. info only — onRampMaxSeqNum - offRampNextSeqNum. No universal healthy value, watch for sustained growth. Empty result (no lanes matched) is UNKNOWN, not zero backlog — and NOT a healthy 'nothing pending' sign either: a healthy plugin still reports 0 per active lane, so absence while under load is the false-idle signature (upstream reader/RPC starving the lane). Corroborate an absence against reader_read_outcome_error / config_poll_failure before reading it as a quiet lane.
panels.title: pending_messages

panels.description: always_emitted: false. warn_if any series>0, ok_if all series==0 (including empty). Chain-throughput ceiling (MaxMerkleTreeSize) being hit.
panels.title: range_truncated

panels.description: always_emitted: false. crit_if any series>0, ok_if all series==0 (including empty). offramp_ahead_of_onramp / onramp_max_zero / offramp_seqnum_regression — documented in-code as stall signals, not routine noise.
panels.title: seqnum_invariant_violation

panels.description: always_emitted: false. warn_if any series>0, ok_if all series==0 (including empty). DON couldn't agree on OffRampNextSeqNum for this chain; looks identical to "no new messages" without this.
panels.title: offramp_consensus_insufficient

panels.description: always_emitted: true. crit_if status=rmn_misconfigured & result==1, info_if status=~skipped_.* & result==1, ok_if status=live & result==1. rmn_misconfigured flags real config drift; skipped_* are expected states. Reported for all four statuses every round — empty result is UNKNOWN, not 'no active lanes', and not a healthy sign either: absence here is the false-idle signature (starved by an upstream reader/RPC issue). Corroborate with reader_read_outcome_error / config_poll_failure.
panels.title: offramp_lane_status

options.content: Cursing is WARN not CRIT deliberately — an active curse is frequently an intentional, already-known state (see `uncommitted-message.md` step4), and paging on expected state trains people to ignore it. `consensus_observation_failed` is the unambiguous CRIT: by construction it can only mean DON-wide FChain agreement failed for this dest chain. If it fires, check `live_oracle_count` before `fchain_read_errors` — an oracle that never started can't emit `fchain_read_errors` at all, so a low oracle count is a root cause `fchain_read_errors` is structurally unable to surface on its own. `consensus_dropped`'s query below excludes `objectName="RMNRemoteConfig"` outright — with RMN disabled in prod it fires constantly and is pure noise, not filtered client-side but removed from the query itself.

panels.description: always_emitted: true. warn_if any series==1, ok_if all series==0. Halts ALL reporting for the dest chain while active; often intentional/incident-flagged — WARN not CRIT. Empty result is UNKNOWN and NOT proof of 'not cursed' — curse state is served from the config-poller cache, so absence alongside rising config_poll_failure / reader_read_outcome_error makes the reading unreliable (a real curse unobserved = false idle).
panels.title: rmn_curse_active

panels.description: always_emitted: true. warn_if any series==1, ok_if all series==0. Per-lane curse; same intentional-vs-bug ambiguity as rmn_curse_active. Empty result is UNKNOWN and not proof the lane is un-cursed — corroborate with reader_read_outcome_error / config_poll_failure before trusting an absence as 'definitely not cursed'. destChainID filter added by the same destChainAttrs fix as the lane_throughput group.
panels.title: source_chain_cursed

panels.description: consensus_observation_failed: always_emitted: false, crit_if result>0 — the only way a whole round fails: DON can't reach 2*fRoleDON+1 agreement on FChain for the dest chain. fchain_read_errors: always_emitted: false, warn_if result>0 — if both fire together, treat as ONE finding (same incident), not two; only reports a *surviving* oracle's own read failures.
panels.title: consensus_observation_failed & fchain_read_errors

panels.description: always_emitted: false. warn_if any series>0, ok_if all series==0 (including empty). Per-key consensus drop breakdown. reason=split on objectName=fChain is H2 (oracles disagree); reason=insufficient_agreement on objectName=fChain together with fchain_read_errors spiking is H1; reason=threshold_not_defined is a config/data mismatch. objectName=RMNRemoteConfig is excluded from this query entirely: with RMN disabled, its remote config is permanently empty so reason=insufficient_agreement fires constantly and is pure noise, never a real finding. Need its raw state anyway? Query ccip_commit_consensus_dropped_total{objectName="RMNRemoteConfig"} directly.
panels.title: consensus_dropped (RMNRemoteConfig excluded)

panels.description: always_emitted: true. Grade manually against $fRoleDON: crit if <2*fRoleDON+1, warn if 2*fRoleDON+1<=result<3*fRoleDON+1, ok if >=3*fRoleDON+1 (leave $fRoleDON blank to just read the raw count). Uses timestamp()-vs-time(), not rate()>0 — confirmed by live testing that rate([5m])>0 stays true for up to 5 minutes after a node actually stops. The ONLY check that can detect "not enough oracles are even running"; if this is low, don't let a flat fchain_read_errors push you toward blaming a split vote instead.
panels.title: live_oracle_count

options.content: `report_transmission_gave_up` is CRIT — one of the most common on-call pages historically. `report_validation_rejected` is split by reason: `stale` alone is INFO, anything else present is WARN, and — being `always_emitted: false` — a fully empty result is OK, not UNKNOWN.

panels.description: always_emitted: false. warn_if any series with reason!=stale>0, info_if only reason=stale>0, ok_if empty or all series==0. reason=stale is usually benign (an overlapping report already landed); other reasons are worth a look.
panels.title: report_validation_rejected

panels.description: always_emitted: false. crit_if any series>0, ok_if all series==0 (including empty). Previously a Warnw with no counter at all. Carries BOTH sourceChainName and destChainID: a single report can cover multiple source chains that resolve independently (pendingSources in merkleroot/outcome.go), so sourceChainName says which lane gave up and destChainID says which destination chain's report it was -- neither is redundant.
panels.title: report_transmission_gave_up

panels.description: always_emitted: false. info only — recorded once per transmission-check attempt; empty result means zero transmission cycles in the window (report as INFO "no data", not UNKNOWN). Rising attempts alongside report_transmission_gave_up firing is the actionable combination.
panels.title: report_transmission_attempts_p95

options.content: Upstream of the whole checklist above: tests whether the plugin is healthy *but being fed empty/partial/stale data*. Shared with execute — every panel below carries `chainID`/`chainFamily`/`chainName`/`chainSelector` (pkg/reader/rcmetrics chainAttrs(), replacing the old bare numeric-selector `chain` label). **Every panel also carries its own `destChainID`/`destChainFamily`/`destChainName`/`destChainSelector`** (a second, dest-scoped chainAttrs() resolved per reader/config-poller instance) — REQUIRED, not cosmetic, confirmed by a real staging incident: a node runs one reader/config-poller instance per destination chain, and more than one instance can independently track the same source chain (two dest-chain lanes both reading Solana collided into one series per (chainID, node_id) without this, silently mixing a healthy lane's fast-refreshing cache with a different, broken lane's stuck one). Every query here filters `destChainID=~"$destChain"` for that reason — see `docs/metrics/reader-metrics.md`. The CRIT here is `config_cache_stale` (sustained: age > 90s means the poller genuinely can't refresh); `config_cache_overwritten_empty` alone is only WARN since a single empty snapshot is benign on its own guard. A finding here firing alongside an outcome check above (`pending_messages` climbing, `consensus_dropped`, a curse/digest-mismatch reading) is the SAME incident with the data-source check as the root cause, not two separate problems.

panels.description: always_emitted: false. warn_if any series>0, ok_if all series==0 (including empty). Consolidated error-leg classification from the observedCCIPReader wrapper -- a query returned a hard error, not just empty/partial (see reader_read_empty/reader_chain_gap for that leg). Filters by chainID=~"$destChain" (destination chain) -- for this one metric chainID and destChainID are always the same value, so either filter works; this is the one exception to this group's chain-selector convention. Split node-local vs DON-wide by csa_public_key before escalating.
panels.title: reader_read_outcome_error

panels.description: always_emitted: false. warn_if any series>0, ok_if all series==0 (including empty). A read returned nothing with no error -- the false-idle primitive. chainID (from pkg/reader/rcmetrics chainAttrs()) is whichever chain that read was about; destChainID=~"$destChain" is REQUIRED to scope this to the lane under investigation (see the panel group's note above); chainSelector on the same series carries the raw numeric selector if needed. Split node-local vs DON-wide by csa_public_key.
panels.title: reader_read_empty

panels.description: always_emitted: false. warn_if any series with state!=returned>0, ok_if all state=returned or empty. Per-chain outcome of a chain read -- actionable states: not_found|disabled|misconfigured|error|invalid|missing|stale|no_accessor|config_error|no_native_token|count_mismatch. count_mismatch = a message read whose count didn't match the requested range (partial data). Query pre-filters state!="returned" so only actionable rows appear; destChainID=~"$destChain" scopes to the lane under investigation.
panels.title: reader_chain_gap (non-returned states)

panels.description: always_emitted: true. crit_if kind=chain & result>90, ok_if all kind=chain result<=90, info for kind=source. SUSTAINED signal: age only climbs across multiple consecutive empty/failed polls (a single intermittent empty is absorbed by the next good poll). >90s (3x the 30s refresh period) means the poller genuinely cannot refresh, so every cached read (RMN config, curse info, config digest, router address) runs on hollow data. destChainID=~"$destChain" is REQUIRED: without it, a chain shared across multiple destination-chain lanes (e.g. Solana read by two different dest chains) can max() together one healthy lane's fresh cache with a different lane's cache stuck for hours -- confirmed on staging, see the panel group's note above.
panels.title: config_cache_stale (age, seconds)

panels.description: always_emitted: true. crit_if time()-result>90, ok_if <=90. Checklist's own query is the raw timestamp (min by (chainID) (ccip_reader_config_poller_last_success_timestamp{destChainID=~"$destChain"})); this panel wraps it in time()-... for direct readability as a staleness duration. Last successful background config poll per chain; a wedged/missing poller goroutine makes every cache silently go stale. destChainID scopes this to the lane under investigation, same reasoning as config_cache_stale.
panels.title: config_poller_liveness (staleness, seconds)

panels.description: always_emitted: false. warn_if any series>0, ok_if all series==0 (including empty). Background config refresh failures, per chain and reason. reason=no_chain_accessor|batch_fetch_failed|no_chain_cache names WHY without needing logs: no_chain_accessor = misconfiguration (no accessor wired up for this chain); batch_fetch_failed = the accessor's fetch call itself errored (RPC/contract-binding problem -- this is the one that fired during the Solana 'no live nodes available' staging incident); no_chain_cache = internal cache-creation failure, should basically never fire. Recorded at the single batchRefreshChainAndSourceConfigs choke point, so on-demand cache-miss fetches count the same as background-refresh ones. destChainID=~"$destChain" is REQUIRED: a rate summed across every destination-chain lane sharing this source chain can look deceptively moderate even when ONE specific lane's poller is failing nearly every cycle -- always scope to the lane you're investigating before judging this against config_cache_stale.
panels.title: config_poll_failure

panels.description: always_emitted: false. warn_if any series>0, ok_if all series==0 (including empty). Accessor returned an EMPTY chain-config snapshot. Per-event this is NOT a page -- the guard refuses to clobber a good cache for a single empty. Only actionable when SUSTAINED, which config_cache_stale (above) already captures; use this one to explain WHY the cache went stale and which chains. If this stays empty while config_cache_stale is climbing for the same chainID/destChainID, that RULES OUT the empty-snapshot path -- look at config_poll_failure (a real accessor error) instead.
panels.title: config_cache_overwritten_empty

options.content: **Alert**: message `$MsgID`, onramp sequence number `$SeqNum`, chain `$sourceChain` (source) → chain `$destChain` (dest), reported in-flight for >15 minutes. Set the variables above (don't have all of them? resolve via `ccip-cli show`, see `docs/runbooks/README.md#identifying-a-ccip-message`), then walk the steps below top to bottom — each stops the moment it has an answer. This is a direct rendering of `docs/runbooks/uncommitted-message.md`'s decision graph; read that doc for full rationale. Outcome vocabulary: **STOP** (resolved), **CONTINUE:\<step\>** (proceed), **REPORT:\<owner\>** (root cause found outside this runbook's scope — hand off, don't act).

`result == 0` → **REPORT:ccip-commit-oncall** (also read the live-oracle-headcount panel below before reporting — turns "not running" into "N of the DON's oracles are actually alive"). `result > 0` → **CONTINUE:step1**. Window is `[1m]`, not `[5m]` — same rate()-extrapolation reasoning as the Liveness panels above.

panels.title: step0 — is the plugin alive at all?

panels.description: condition: result==0. Always run the followup (live oracle headcount) before reporting — confirmed by live testing that a bare "not running" reads as unsatisfyingly generic on its own.
panels.title: step0 — plugin_heartbeat & live oracle headcount

options.content: `result > $SeqNum` → **STOP** — a root covering it already landed on the offramp; commit plugin's job is done, hand off to exec on-call for delivery status. `result <= $SeqNum` → **CONTINUE:step2**. `destChainID=~"$destChain"` is required on this and every per-lane query below — without it you're reading this lane across every destination chain sharing this datasource, not just the one under investigation.

panels.title: step1 — is this even a commit-plugin problem?

panels.description: condition: result > $SeqNum.
panels.title: step1 — offramp_next_seq_num

options.content: `result < $SeqNum` → **REPORT:chain-infra-oncall** — onramp read is lagging; check the errors-by-reason panel below (no_bindings/timeout/rpc_error/msg_count_mismatch/hash_error/address_lookup_error). Source-chain read/infra issue, not commit logic. `result >= $SeqNum` → **CONTINUE:step2b**.

panels.title: step2 — has the plugin observed it on-chain yet?

panels.description: condition: result < $SeqNum.
panels.title: step2 — onramp_max_seq_num

panels.description: Only relevant if step2 fired (onramp read lagging).
panels.title: step2 followup — merkleroot_observation_errors by reason

options.content: The onramp has been observed, but the DON still has to agree on the source-chain values that go into the merkle root. `any result > 0` → **REPORT:ccip-commit-oncall** — consensus_dropped reason=split means disagreeing oracles, reason=insufficient_agreement means too few oracles observed the key, reason=threshold_not_defined is a config/data mismatch; offramp_consensus_insufficient means the DON couldn't agree on OffRampNextSeqNums for this lane. The message cannot advance until the disagreement resolves. All flat → **CONTINUE:step2c**.

panels.title: step2b — can the DON agree on this chain's per-chain values?

panels.description: condition: any result > 0.
panels.title: step2b — per-chain consensus_dropped & offramp_consensus_insufficient

options.content: The on/offramp gauges and consensus signals are *outcomes* — they can't tell "plugin is broken" apart from "plugin is fine but fed empty/partial data." Any `read_empty`/non-`returned` `chain_gap` `> 0`, or `config_cache_age_seconds{kind="chain"}` sustained above ~90s → **REPORT:chain-infra-oncall**, the data layer is degrading (a reader/chain-infra problem, not a commit-plugin defect); split single-node vs DON-wide by `csa_public_key` first. All flat → **CONTINUE:step3**. `chainID`/`chainFamily`/`chainName`/`chainSelector` below (pkg/reader/rcmetrics chainAttrs()) describe whichever chain a read is about, shared with execute; every panel here ALSO filters `destChainID=~"$destChain"` (a second, dest-scoped chainAttrs()) -- REQUIRED, not optional, since a node runs one reader instance per destination chain and more than one instance can independently track the same source chain (confirmed on staging) — see `docs/metrics/reader-metrics.md`. This is a data-layer *gate* placed before the consensus/transmission tree, exactly where a silently-empty reader would otherwise be misattributed to the plugin.

panels.title: step2c — is the problem upstream in the data source instead?

panels.description: condition: any result > 0.
panels.title: step2c — reader_read_empty (this lane's queries)

panels.description: condition: any result > 0. Actionable states: not_found|disabled|misconfigured|error|invalid|missing|stale|count_mismatch.

targets.expr: sum by (query, chainID, state) (rate(ccip_reader_chain_gap_total{query=~"NextSeqNum|MsgsBetweenSeqNums|GetChainsFeeComponents|GetChainFeePriceUpdate", state!="returned", destChainID=~"$destChain"}[5m]))

panels.title: step2c — reader_chain_gap (non-returned states)

panels.description: condition: kind="chain" sustained above ~90s (3x refresh period) — a single intermittent empty poll isn't enough.
panels.title: step2c — config_cache_age_seconds

options.content: Incrementing → destination-chain-wide consensus failure, jump to **Scenario 3** below. Flat → **CONTINUE:step4**.

panels.title: step3 — is the round producing outcomes at all?

panels.description: condition: result > 0.
panels.title: step3 — consensus_observation_failed

options.content: Any `== 1` → **REPORT:curse-owner** — found it; likely intentional/incident-flagged. Curse state is served from the config-poller cache: if `config_cache_age_seconds{kind="chain"}` is high (see step2c panel above), the curse reading itself may be stale — say so when reporting. All `0` → **CONTINUE:step5**. RMN-signature branches (signed-roots-dropped, chain quorum, Byzantine root disagreement) are intentionally absent: `RMNEnabled` is hardcoded off in production, so those paths are dead code — cursing is the one RMN-adjacent signal still live.

panels.title: step4 — is chain A or B cursed?

panels.description: condition: result==1.
panels.title: step4 — RMN global curse

panels.description: condition: result==1.
panels.title: step4 — RMN destination curse

panels.description: condition: result==1.
panels.title: step4 — source chain cursed

options.content: Incrementing/maxed → jump to **Scenario 2** below. Otherwise → likely just backlog size — report `pending_messages` and an ETA estimate from round cadence, and stop.

panels.title: step5 — is a report being built but never landing?

panels.description: condition: report_transmission_gave_up result > 0.
panels.title: step5 — report_transmission_gave_up & pending_messages

options.content:
**A — never transmitted (rejected pre-send).** Branch by `reason` in the panel below: `config_digest_mismatch`→config sync issue (cross-check config_digest_mismatch above); `config_digest_check_error`→RPC/read error checking the digest, chain-infra-oncall, not a real mismatch; `stale`→often benign, **STOP**, re-check step1; `dest_not_supported`→transmission-schedule/config bug; `dest_support_check_error`→RPC/read error, chain-infra-oncall; `cursed`→converges with step4; `cursed_check_error`→RPC/read error, chain-infra-oncall, don't conflate with step4's cursed=1; `empty_root` / `invalid_seqnum_range`→report-builder produced an invalid report -- before blaming the processor, check the reader-corroboration panel below for a partial/empty read on `MsgsBetweenSeqNums` for this lane around the same time; `decode_report` / `decode_report_info`→codec/chainlink-common version skew; `root_blessing_mismatch`→on-chain blessing validation failed; **any other reason**→do NOT guess which of the above it's "close enough to" — report the exact string and rate, say this runbook has no mapping for it yet. All flat → **CONTINUE:scenario2b**.

**B — transmitted, reverted/stuck on-chain.** *(automatable: false)* Check chain B's TXM/tx-sender dashboards for the assigned transmitter (nonce gap, underpriced gas, wallet balance, revert reason).

**C — actually succeeded, read is lagging.** *(automatable: false)* `offramp_next_seq_num` is sourced from this plugin's own chain-B reader; cross-check chain B's block explorer / chain-reader health directly before escalating further.

panels.title: Deep dive — Scenario 2: report transmission stuck (step5)

panels.description: condition: any reason count > 0.
panels.title: Scenario 2 — report_validation_rejected{phase="should_transmit"} by reason

panels.description: Only relevant if scenario2 fired with reason=empty_root or invalid_seqnum_range. chain_gap{state="count_mismatch"} in particular can manufacture invalid_seqnum_range without any processor bug. Any firing for this lane around the same time → reader-layer issue, not a processor bug.
panels.title: Scenario 2 followup — reader corroboration for empty_root/invalid_seqnum_range

options.content:
Grounded in `getConsensusObservation` (`merkleroot/outcome.go`): the *only* way the whole round fails is the DON not reaching 2·fRoleDON+1 agreement on a single FChain value for the **destination chain** — every other field degrades gracefully per-chain.

**Destination-chain-wide check first.** If only `$sourceChain`'s series is climbing in the panel below while others into the same dest are flat → this branch is wrong, **back to step4/step5**. Confirmed dest-wide → continue.

**H0 — not enough oracles are even running.** *(Check before H1/H2 — a distinct failure mode neither of them can detect.)* If `$fRoleDON` known: `< 2*fRoleDON+1` → **this is the answer, REPORT:ccip-commit-oncall, stop here** — don't let a flat H1 push you toward H2, they check a different failure mode. `>= 2*fRoleDON+1` → continue to H1/H2. If `$fRoleDON` unknown → report the raw count as context and continue, but treat H1/H2's conclusion as lower-confidence.

**H1 — too few oracles could read it.** Spiking broadly across oracles → **REPORT:home-chain-infra-oncall**, home-chain RPC/read outage. Corroborate with the reader-layer panel below, grouped by node: firing across (nearly) every `csa_public_key` for the same query is DON-wide data-source failure, not a split vote; one or two nodes only is that node's RPC. Both flat → corroborates H2 instead.

**H2 — oracles disagree (split vote).** Confirm with consensus_dropped{objectName=fChain, reason=split}; corroborate with config_digest_mismatch flipping for a subset of oracles around the same time → **REPORT:ccip-commit-oncall**. If H0 couldn't rule out insufficient participation (fRoleDON unknown), treat this as low-confidence, not a firm diagnosis.

panels.title: Deep dive — Scenario 3: consensus never completes (step3)

panels.description: condition: only $sourceChain's series is climbing, others flat → branch is wrong, back to step4/step5. Deliberately no sourceChainName filter -- comparing every lane into $destChain is the point.
panels.title: Scenario 3 — pending_messages across ALL lanes into $destChain
